title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. L is a totally ordered set. M is the set of 'cells' of L: points x in L and open intervals I_{a,b} with a<b. Each cell X has a boundary δX: δx={x} and δI_{ab}={a,b}. The closure X̃ is X together with its faces (on a point, X̃={x}; on an interval, X̃={I_ab,a,b}). The face relation is ⊲ / ⊴. M carries a strict order < with a < I_{ab} < b; it orders cells left to right, so a face is comparable with the cell it bounds. The previous page defined X|∘|Y as 'X<Y or Y<X', i.e. {X,Y} is a 2-element flag (chain) of (M,<). |·| on this page seems to play the same role (strict comparability).

This page specialises the general 'atelier' relation ≴ to this 1-dimensional situation. Roughly, X ≴ Y means X and Y are 'non-overlapping': their closures meet only along common faces, so that after removing the common part the closures are separated.

Lemma. If X≠Y, then X̃∩Ỹ = δX∩δY, which has 0 or 1 element.

Proposition. X ≴ Y ⇔ X=Y or X|·|Y, i.e. {X,Y} is a flag (chain) of M.

Proof. Assume X≠Y.
(a) If X̃∩Ỹ=∅, then X ≴ Y means X̃|·|Ỹ (separated). Since the intersection is empty, this is equivalent to comparability X<Y or Y<X.
(b) If X̃∩Ỹ={b}, there are two sub-cases.
- If one cell is a face of the other (X⊲Y or Y⊲X), then both X ≴ Y and comparability hold.
- Otherwise both are intervals sharing the endpoint b, so X=I_{ab} and Y=I_{bc} with a<b<c. Then (X̃∖{b}) and (Ỹ∖{b}) are separated, so X ≴ Y; and X<Y also holds. QED.

Corollary. A subset Φ⊂M is a prefigure (pairwise ≴) iff it is totally ordered by ≤. The next page adds that figures are the finite chains that are also closed under faces.

In modern terms, this is the combinatorics of finite subdivisions of a linearly ordered set into vertices and open edges, i.e. 1-dimensional cell complexes on an ordered line. Prefigures correspond to chains of the 'cell order', and figures to subcomplexes that are segments of subdivisions. It is a test case for Grothendieck's abstract axioms (Mag 3, Mag 4) for 'ateliers' of figures.
errors: The argument is sketchy but essentially correct, given the definitions on the previous page.
In case (b) the text writes 'X,Y ∉ X∩Y' for 'neither is a face of the other'; the intended meaning is clear.

Case (a) asserts without detail that separation of the closures is equivalent to <-comparability. This is true: a point strictly inside an interval, or two overlapping intervals, are neither separated nor comparable. But the check is left implicit.

ideas.what: Cell order on points and intervals of a totally ordered set, with flags/chains characterising compatible families of cells
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / cell order of subdivisions of a line; chains in a poset as 1-dimensional subdivisions

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'ateliers' of figures with a non-overlap relation ≴ and axioms Mag 3/4, tested on the 1-dimensional example
ideas.modern_name: Close in spirit to o-minimal cell decompositions / tame topology (combinatorial foundations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's tame-topology programme (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); o-minimality by van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse discusses tame topology in spirit only; the 'ateliers' formalism is not published as far as I know

missed.claim: The 1986 'ateliers' formalism is an axiomatic theory of figures/prefigures meant to underlie a combinatorial tame topology. This page verifies it in the 1-dimensional ordered case, where figures are face-closed finite chains of the cell order. The general programme seems undeveloped in the literature.
missed.quote: Pour qu'une partie Φ de M soit une préfigure de M (i.e. Φ soit une figure) il f. et s. qu'elle soit totalement ordonnée par ≤.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible comparison with o-minimal cell decompositions and with combinatorial models of stratified spaces. However, this page's own content is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification in a toy 1-dimensional model of an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself ('ateliers') is little known, but nothing on this page is a nontrivial new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Gr.(M)' in the Proposition is more likely 'Drap_≤(M)' or 'Drap(M)' (the set of flags), consistent with the previous page.
'(par là, intersection)' probably reads '(par hyp. sur intersection)' or similar.
The relation symbol written ≴ is a 'not less-or-greater'-type symbol (non-overlap relation) as drawn in the image.
